mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 4.0% but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.0% signals labor market deterioration that triggers risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.0% but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market defined by high payroll growth (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) drives corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through joint market sentiment effects.
failure_condition: PAYEMS > 150,000 and UNRATE < 3.5% but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 300), additional federal funds rate hikes compress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Trigger condition met but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index, 2017=100) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 but S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts (HOUST) below 1,400,000 units indicates weak residential demand that depresses consumer confidence and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1400.0 but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher retail sales level (RSAFS) reflects strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic conditions.
failure_condition: RSAFS above 50th percentile of historical values but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing contraction (INDPRO < 100), a further decline in industrial production intensifies recessionary expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
